subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in headless browser for reliable web access without external dependencies

question: What product shape should OpenClaw use for browser-backed web access: integrate rendered extraction into web_fetch/web_search, keep browser automation as a separate explicit tool with stronger guidance, or delegate advanced extraction to plugins/providers?
rationale: The current gap is real, but choosing where rendered extraction lives determines security boundaries, plugin/core ownership, config surface, session storage, proxy semantics, and user-visible defaults; automation cannot safely choose that product contract.

options.title: Stage Browser-Backed Extraction
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical design tracker and approve narrower follow-up work for rendered extraction, session/proxy policy, benchmarked acceptance criteria, and security review.

options.title: Keep Tools Separate
options.body: Keep web_fetch/web_search as lightweight HTTP/provider tools and improve routing/docs so agents switch to the existing browser tool for JS-heavy or login-required pages.

options.title: Plugin/Provider First
options.body: Require advanced rendered extraction to ship as a plugin or provider contract first, extending core only for missing generic plugin APIs.

recommendation.title: Stage Browser-Backed Extraction
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical design tracker and approve narrower follow-up work for rendered extraction, session/proxy policy, benchmarked acceptance criteria, and security review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history across bundled browser ownership, browser docs, and current web-fetch/browser boundary wording.
